content:
alex: heads-up — Acme escalated a weird cascade during a burst. timeline: ~2026-10-12T10:12Z they sent a traffic spike that hit eu-west capacity, we failed them over to us-east, they saw a bunch of 429s and a handful of 401s. customer is really sensitive to both latency and sudden throttles, so they raised a P1. attaching repro & logs below.

maria: copy. do we have raw request ids / headers? can we correlate to routing decision? @ryan any quick theory? :thinking_face: 

alex: pasted minimal log slice — note the routing header and the 429s after fallback: 

```
[2026-10-12T10:12:04Z] req_id=acme-req-0001 region=eu-west pool=dedicated-eu status=429 reason=capacity_exhausted fallback=us-east X-Region-Fallback=true
[2026-10-12T10:12:05Z] req_id=acme-req-0002 region=eu-west pool=dedicated-eu status=200
[2026-10-12T10:12:06Z] req_id=acme-req-0003 region=eu-west pool=dedicated-eu status=429 reason=capacity_exhausted fallback=us-east X-Region-Fallback=true
[2026-10-12T10:12:06Z] req_id=acme-req-0003-forwarded region=us-east pool=shared-us status=429 reason=regional_throttle
[2026-10-12T10:12:07Z] req_id=acme-req-0004 region=eu-west pool=dedicated-eu status=401 reason=auth_invalid_token forwarded_to=us-east
```

alex: the interesting bit — the forwarded request got a 401 in us-east. token header looked like: `Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-eu-...` — maybe the token is bound to region or keyset mismatch.

ryan: that matches an SRE investigation I did last month: fallback requests are forwarded as-is and the auth check in the destination region validates against the destination's active keyset. if the customer's token was minted for dedicated-eu and we don't mirror key-id mappings to shared-us, auth can fail. separately, regional_throttle is a per-region rate limit (applies to incoming tokens and project id). when we fail over, those requests hit the destination region's quotas and can be throttled there as well. so two separate failure modes: quota exhaustion in eu -> failover -> destination region also throttles -> some requests rejected for auth.

sara: ah — so the sequence is: dedicated pool full -> router marks fallback -> request forwarded to shared pool in other region -> auth check fails for some tokens OR destination rate limiter hits per-customer cross-region cap -> 429/401 mix. that would explain mixed error types.

jen: any repro we can run from support side to show customer? alex, can you paste a curl that reproduces the path?

alex: yes — quick repro (non-destructive) using region hint header we use for testing: 

```
# run 60 concurrent short requests with region hint to trigger failover path
for i in {1..60}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-eu-XXXX" \
    -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west" \
    -H "X-Client-Project: acme-project" \
    "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" &
done; wait
```

alex: results on my test run: ~38x 429 (mix of capacity_exhausted & regional_throttle) and 4x 401 with `auth_invalid_token`.

ingest-bot: attached ingestion trace for req_id=acme-req-0003 (trace link: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/acme-req-0003)

maria: ok that's actionable. short term we should: 
- confirm whether customer tokens are region-scoped (ask auth team)
- if tokens are global, check why key-id mapping missing in us-east for dedicated-eu tokens
- check destination region quota windows for acme-project around 10:12Z (billing/usage)

ops-oncall: I'll take triage. creating incident INC-2026-ACME-089, tagging SRE and Auth. assigning to @ryan.

ryan: on it. initial findings: destination region had a recent quota reset and a small cap for shared pools -> their burst was enough to trip both dedicated-eu eviction and shared-us protective throttle. Also found configuration mismatch: a cache refresh job that mirrors service key metadata to shared regions failed briefly at 10:10Z. that explains 401s — destination couldn't validate some token key ids.

billing-bot: billing note: cross-region routing caused ~12k additional tokens served from shared-us; projected short-term overage ~$125 for Acme (we will override if we decide to waive due to platform routing issue).

sara: mitigation plan (short term):
1) Ops: temporarily raise per-customer protective throttle for shared-us for Acme (window 30m) to avoid immediate 429s during troubleshooting. (ops-oncall: can you do?)
2) Auth: backfill missing key metadata in us-east so forwarded tokens validate.
3) Router: disable immediate fallback for Acme in eu-west for next 30m (force queueing / retry semantics instead of cross-region).

ryan: done step 2 (backfilled). auth now returns 200 for previously failing token ids. started rolling keycache resync across regions.

ops-oncall: raised Acme shared-us protective throttle by 3x for 45m, added guardrails.

alex: after fixes I re-ran the curl loop: 60 requests -> 6x 429 (all capacity_exhausted in eu-west; none 401) and latency improved on retries. customer on Slack says errors dropped significantly but wants root cause & bill impact.

maria: follow-ups for postmortem: 
- root cause: combination of dedicated pool saturation + missing key cache in destination region + destination region protective throttle being conservative.
- immediate resolution: keycache backfill, temporary throttle bump, router policy change.
- customer impact: transient 429s + few 401s during failover window.
- billing: billing-bot flagged $125 overage; propose to credit it due to platform routing issue.

billing-bot: proposed credit: full $125. awaiting finance approval.

jen: docs/engineering note: we should add a test that simulates a 2-region failover with keycache delay to ensure no auth regressions. also add a router flag to rewrite/attach proxied-token headers that destination accepts when we intentionally failover (requires auth sign-off).

ryan: next steps (owners):
- ryan (SRE): add alert when keycache mirror job fails more than 2x in 10m.
- sara (platform): add router toggle to opt into token normalization for trusted dedicated->shared failover.
- ops-oncall: revert throttle bump after 45m and monitor.
- alex/maria: follow up with customer success to describe remediation & bill credit.

alex: customer message draft (I'll send after finance confirms credit): 
> Hi team, we saw a brief routing/validation issue during your burst. We've fixed authentication mirroring and temporarily adjusted routing to prevent repeated cross-region throttles. We'll apply a $125 credit to cover extra tokens served. Let me know if you'd like a call. :pray: 

maria: thanks everyone — closing P1 after postmortem and confirm credit. capturing in INC-2026-ACME-089. closing thread here but keeping notes in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
